name: AI Score
evidence: Headline: UK startup AI Score raises $5.4M to scale its enterprise AI governance platform

Summary: London-based AI governancecompany AI Score has raised $5.4 million in seed funding to further develop itsplatform for managing the use of generative and agentic AI acrossorganisations. The round was l...
Headline: London’s AI Score raises €4.6 million to help businesses keep AI agents under control

assessment.whatTheyDo: AI Score is a London-based B2B SaaS startup building a real-time governance/control-plane platform that gives enterprises visibility and policy control over their use of generative and agentic AI tools.
matchedInterests: Agent frameworks, evaluation, and LLM tooling
concerns: Headquartered in London, UK — materially harder for a US-based candidate to join (visa/relocation/timezone), and no evidence of a US presence or remote-in-US hiring.

No named CTO or technical co-founder found; the visible leadership (CEO from national security/NCSC background, COO an ex-City lawyer) skews policy/legal rather than engineering, so founder technical depth is unproven.

No open engineering roles currently listed on the company's careers channel (Welcome to the Jungle), and only 1-20 employees per LinkedIn — unclear if they are actively hiring engineers at all right now.
No public technical detail (architecture, stack, integrations) found to substantiate product depth beyond marketing copy.
assessment.rationale: The company sits adjacent to a top-weighted interest (agentic AI tooling/governance) and is a small, real operating company with staged, modest fundraising rather than a hype-driven mega-seed — but the founding team's public backgrounds are security-policy and legal, not engineering, and there's no evidence of open technical roles or a US/remote footprint, which are the two biggest levers for this person's fit as an engineering hire.
assessment.summary: AI Score is a London seed-stage startup (founded 2025) building an 'AI governance control plane' that monitors and manages generative/agentic AI usage inside enterprises, addressing compliance and safety risk as agentic AI spreads. It just raised $5.4M (£4m) in seed funding led by Fuel Ventures, following a ~$1M pre-seed in late 2025, and is advised by former GCHQ Director Sir Jeremy Fleming.
assessment.product: A real-time monitoring and policy-enforcement platform ('control plane') that gives enterprises visibility into how generative and agentic AI tools are used across their organization, flagging compliance and safety risks against internal policy, serving sectors including financial services, legal, and consumer.
assessment.team: CEO Alex Harland, who was on the founding team of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC); COO Benita Tibb, previously a City (London) lawyer; Jonathan Kewley also associated with the company. The startup was incubated within GALLOS Technologies, a venture studio for security/defence/resilience companies. Advised by Sir Jeremy Fleming, former Director of GCHQ. No technical co-founder or CTO was identified in available sources.
assessment.funding: $5.4M (£4m) seed round announced ~2026-09-04, led by Fuel Ventures, with participation from GALLOS Technologies, Alan Morgan (co-founder of MMC Ventures, early Funding Circle/Tide investor), and Mo El Husseiny (Managing Partner, Ventura Capital). This follows a ~$1M / £761k pre-seed round in November 2025.
redFlags: No visible technical/engineering leadership publicly named despite the product being a data/monitoring platform.
Incubated inside a venture studio (GALLOS Technologies), which can mean less founder-driven autonomy than an independently founded company.
No current open roles listed on its careers page as of this research.
greenFlags: Staged, disciplined fundraising (small pre-seed followed by a modest seed) rather than a large round with no shipped product.
Credible early-stage investor base (Fuel Ventures, MMC Ventures co-founder) and a high-profile advisor (former GCHQ Director).
Targets a real and growing enterprise pain point (agentic AI governance/compliance) rather than a purely thin GPT-wrapper play.
Very small team (1-20 employees), which would offer high leverage to an early engineering hire if roles do open up.

name: AIR
evidence: Headline: AIR raises $50M to help companies vet the skills and add-ons AI agents use
Summary: AIR's platform can discover agents running at a company, continuously vets any skills and add-ons they use, and blocks any unwanted behavior.

assessment.whatTheyDo: AIR Security builds an inline security/firewall platform that discovers AI agents running inside a company, continuously vets the skills, plugins, and MCP add-ons those agents use, and blocks risky behavior.
assessment.headquarters: Israel (with newly started US hiring; exact city not disclosed in press)
matchedInterests: Agent frameworks, evaluation, and LLM tooling
concerns: Headquartered in Israel, not the US — press indicates 'we started hiring employees in the United States' but no US office city or scope is confirmed, so this is materially harder to join than a domestic company without relocation or a strong remote setup.

$50M raised across two rounds within the company's first ~6 months (founded Feb 2026) is a very large early raise; mitigated by the fact they already report 20+ customers and a live, multi-component product rather than pure vaporware.
No careers page or specific open roles could be found — could not verify current hiring for engineering vs. GTM roles.
assessment.rationale: Technical founders with strong offensive-security pedigree (Unit 8200), a genuinely shipped product with named components (Control, Filter, Defend, Marketplace) and original published research, plus 20+ paying customers give real evidence this is a substantial technical company at ~40 people, which is high-leverage. But the theme (AI agent security/cybersecurity) is only mid-weight in this profile, the company is HQ'd outside the US which meaningfully complicates joining, and no open engineering roles were confirmed, so this lands as a solid-but-not-exceptional match rather than a top-tier one.
assessment.summary: AIR Security is an AI-agent security startup founded in February 2026 by Yair Saban (CEO) and Niv Hoffman (CTO), both Unit 8200 veterans, that emerged from stealth on 2026-09-01 with $50M raised across two seed rounds. It sells an 'inline firewall' that vets and governs the skills, plugins, and MCP servers AI agents use inside enterprises, and already has 20+ customers including large regulated enterprises.
assessment.product: A four-part platform (AIR Control, AIR Filter, AIR Defend, AIR Marketplace) that discovers AI agents in a company's environment, vets their skills/plugins/MCP add-ons before and during use, provides runtime protection, and offers a marketplace of pre-vetted add-ons — sold to enterprises, with strongest traction in financial services and pharma.
assessment.team: Co-founded by CEO Yair Saban and CTO Niv Hoffman, who met roughly a decade ago in Israel's Unit 8200 intelligence corps doing offensive cybersecurity; joined by Ryan Knisley (former CISO at Disney and Costco) as Chief Strategy Officer. ~40 employees, primarily in Israel, with US hiring recently started.
assessment.funding: $50M total across two seed rounds closed weeks apart: $10M led by Sequoia, then $40M led by Greenoaks, with participation from Swish Ventures, Netz, and angels including Zach Frankel (Cognition), Yinon Costica (Wiz co-founder), Ofir Ehrlich (Eon co-founder), and others.
redFlags: HQ in Israel with US presence still nascent, adding relocation/visa/time-zone friction for a US-based candidate.
Very large seed funding ($50M) only ~6 months after founding is a scale of raise more typical of later-stage rounds.
Crowded, well-funded competitive space — Zenity raised $125M Series C and Noma raised $100M Series B, both ahead of or larger than AIR's raise.
greenFlags: Founders have deep, relevant technical/security backgrounds (Unit 8200 offensive cybersecurity) rather than pure business pedigree.
Real, shipped, multi-component product plus original published security research (e.g., an 'MCPJacking' vulnerability disclosure), not just a pitch deck.
20+ paying customers already, about a quarter of them large enterprises, within months of founding.
Small team (~40 people) relative to funding raised, suggesting individual engineers would have real leverage.

name: Atira
evidence: Headline: Atira raises $17.5M to bring AI orchestration to industrial sales

Summary: Munich-based AIcompany Atira has raised $15 million in seed funding to expand its platform forautomating industrial sales engineering. The round was led by Accel, withparticipation from UVC, Fortino, ...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Atira builds an AI orchestration platform ("the commercial brain") that automates industrial sales engineering — reading RFQs, flagging spec risks, and generating quotes/proposals by integrating with a manufacturer's CRM, ERP, and CPQ systems.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Munich, Germany with in-office (not remote) roles — materially harder for a US-based engineer to join without relocation or visa sponsorship, and no evidence of US hiring or remote-friendly policy.
CEO's background is commercial (ex-Palantir commercial/deployment lead), not engineering — technical depth is concentrated in the CTO alone, which is thinner founder-engineering bench than ideal.

$17.5M total raised (incl. a previously undisclosed $2.5M pre-seed) is a fairly large seed stage; mitigated somewhat by the fact they already have ~15 paying customers and quantified usage, not just a pitch deck.
assessment.rationale: Real product with paying industrial customers (ABB E-mobility, Chiron, Robel) and quantified impact (80% faster quoting, 95 hours saved per quotation) is strong evidence against hype-only positioning, and the small team (~15, growing to ~24) means genuine leverage for an early engineer. The score is held back mainly by geography — Munich-only, in-office roles are a real barrier for this US-based candidate — and by a founding team where only one of two founders (the CTO, ex-Google ML) has deep technical depth.
assessment.summary: Atira is a Munich-based startup (founded Nov 2024) building AI agents that automate industrial sales engineering — parsing complex RFQs and generating technical quotes/proposals for manufacturers. It just disclosed $17.5M total funding ($15M seed led by Accel plus a previously unannounced $2.5M pre-seed), has real customers with measurable results, and is hiring, but is based and hiring in-office in Germany with no apparent remote/US track.
assessment.product: An AI orchestration/agent platform that sits between a manufacturer's CRM and ERP, reading customer requests, flagging unmet specs, and drafting technical/commercial proposals for complex built-to-order industrial products; agents escalate to human experts via Microsoft Teams when needed.
assessment.team: Co-founded Nov 2024 by Florian Diegruber (CEO, former commercial/deployment lead at Palantir working with German automotive manufacturers) and August DuMont Schütte (CTO, former machine learning engineer at Google). Team grew from 4 employees at the start of the year to roughly 15 currently, with ~9 more hires imminent.
assessment.funding: $15M seed led by Accel, with UVC Partners, Fortino Ventures, BOOOM, and angels including Ann-Kristin Achleitner, Whirlpool CEO Marc Bitzer, Markus Flik, and Celonis co-CEO Bastian Nominacher; plus a previously undisclosed $2.5M pre-seed, for $17.5M total.
techStack: agent harnesses/runtimes and evals (per their own careers messaging)
integrations with CRM, ERP, and CPQ systems
Microsoft Teams integration for human-in-the-loop review
redFlags: In-office-only hiring in Munich with no visible remote or US roles.
Only one of two co-founders has a hands-on engineering background.
greenFlags: ~15 paying customers since a Nov 2025 launch, including named industrial names (ABB E-mobility, Chiron Group, Robel), with 5 customers already at 100+ users each — real usage, not vaporware.
Small team (~15-24 people) despite $17.5M raised, suggesting high per-engineer leverage.
Technical CTO with Google ML engineering background; product work explicitly involves agent harnesses, runtimes, and evals rather than a thin prompt wrapper.

name: Atorie
evidence: Headline: Fashion startup Atorie raises $9.5M to bring consumers luxury goods without the markup
Summary: Shoppers can visit the Atorie website and buy handbags or clothes made from the same material — and coming from the same factory — that manufacturers use in high-end goods.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Atorie is a direct-to-consumer marketplace selling handbags, apparel, and accessories made in the same factories/materials as luxury brands (e.g. Prada, RRL, Arc'teryx), cutting out brand markup, with light AI features for trend analysis, demand prediction, and outfit recommendations.
concerns: Core business is a fashion/dupe e-commerce brand — supply chain, merchandising, and marketing look like the primary value drivers, not software; AI features (trend analysis, outfit-building agents) appear to be product add-ons rather than the core technical moat.

No evidence found of current senior/staff engineering hiring — the only specific open role located (via Fashionista, Nov 2024) was a Senior Marketing Associate, which is a weaker signal per this person's stated preference.

CEO's background is business/creator-platform (Snipfeed), not deeply technical; CTO has an AI background (ex-Google) but no public technical writing, stack details, or engineering team size were found.
assessment.rationale: Real product with real revenue (~$5M in 2025, reportedly scaling toward $55M+ ARR in 2026) and a reasonably sized $9.5M seed, so this isn't a hype-only raise — that's a genuine positive. But it matches only the lowest-priority-fit of this person's top themes (consumer marketplace) and reads as a retail/DTC brand with AI-flavored features rather than a technology company where an engineer would have deep product leverage; no evidence of active senior engineering hiring pulls it further down.
assessment.summary: Atorie is an LA-based luxury-fashion marketplace, founded 2024 by Redouane Ramdani (previously founded creator platform Snipfeed, sold to a PE firm) and CTO Luis Angulo (ex-Google AI). It just raised a $9.5M seed from a16z Speedrun, Night Capital, and Lightspeed's Jeremy Liew, and claims real revenue traction. It's a legitimate operating consumer brand, but likely more retail-operations-heavy than engineering-heavy, and no evidence surfaced of active technical hiring.
assessment.product: E-commerce marketplace selling luxury-grade apparel/handbags/accessories sourced from the same factories/materials used by high-end brands, plus AI-driven trend prediction, demand forecasting, and shopping/outfit recommendation agents on the site.
assessment.team: Co-founder/CEO Redouane Ramdani, grew up around family in luxury manufacturing in France, previously founded creator platform Snipfeed (scaled to ~$100M GMV, 300k+ creators, acquired by a PE firm in 2024). Co-founder/CTO Luis Angulo, described as a former Google AI specialist.
assessment.funding: $9.5M seed round announced August 27, 2026, per TechCrunch. Investors named: a16z Speedrun, Night Capital, and Lightspeed Venture Partners' Jeremy Liew.
redFlags: No confirmed evidence of engineering hiring; only publicly found open role (marketing) suggests early go-to-market emphasis over engineering buildout.
greenFlags: Already generating meaningful revenue (~$5M in 2025) with a claimed path to $55M+ 2026 ARR — a real, shipped, revenue-generating product rather than a pre-launch idea.
US-based (Los Angeles, CA) headquarters, matching the person's preferred geography.
Seed size ($9.5M) is proportionate to traction rather than an oversized pre-product raise.

name: Backbone

assessment.whatTheyDo: Backbone is a Belgian pre-seed startup building an AI platform that automates quality and compliance operations (supplier tracking, document control, incident management, certification mapping) for food and beverage producers.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Belgium, not the US — materially harder to join due to visa/relocation/time-zone, per the person's geography preference.

assessment.summary: Backbone (usebackbone.ai) is a Ghent/Brussels-area, Belgium-based startup founded in October 2025 by Louis Opsomer, Siska Lannoo and Julien Steel — all former managers at Henchman, a Ghent legal-tech startup Opsomer co-founded and sold to LexisNexis in 2024. assessment.product: An AI platform for food & beverage quality/QA teams that ingests documents, supplier data, and lab results, maps them to standards like BRCGS, IFS, and FSSC 22000, and surfaces compliance gaps and risks in real time, replacing manual spreadsheet-based tracking.
assessment.team: Founded by Louis Opsomer, Siska Lannoo, and Julien Steel, all former managers at Henchman (Ghent legal-drafting startup); Opsomer co-founded Henchman and it was acquired by LexisNexis in 2024, giving the founding team a credible prior technical/startup track record. assessment.funding: €4M pre-seed (announced ~2026-09-03) led by Pitchdrive, with PROfounders Capital, Passion Capital, 100IN, and a group of Belgian food-industry families (including Agristo and Darta) participating. Earlier informal backing came from Henchman's founders (Gilles Mattelin and Jorn Vanysacker) via the 100IN fund before Backbone had a shipped product.
redFlags: Non-US headquarters increases friction for a US-based candidate to actually join.
Careers page (hosted on Notion) could not be read for real role listings, so hiring seniority/level is unverified.
greenFlags: Already has a real, paying customer base (Zoutman, Greenway, Azingro, Euromeat, Budelpack, Royal Taste, J&K Confectionery) across three countries at pre-seed stage — not just a concept.
Founding team has direct prior experience building and successfully exiting a startup (Henchman → LexisNexis).
Applied AI in a concrete operational vertical (food safety/compliance) rather than a thin generic wrapper.

name: Conveo
evidence: Headline: Conveo raises $50M to scale its AI-powered consumer intelligence platform

Summary: Consumerresearch technology company Conveo has raised $50 million in Series A fundingto expand in the US and develop its platform into a broader consumerintelligence infrastructure for enterprises. Th...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Conveo (conveo.ai) builds an AI-powered platform that runs and analyzes video/voice consumer research interviews at scale for enterprise product, marketing, and research teams.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Antwerp, Belgium — outside the US, which is a materially harder join unless targeting one of their NYC/SF roles specifically.
Already ~80-90 employees at Series A, larger than an ideal 'high-leverage' early team.
Open roles skew heavily toward sales/GTM/ops relative to engineering, suggesting growth may currently be sales-led.

assessment.rationale: Conveo is a real, substantial company: 400+ enterprise customers including Google, Unilever, P&G and Canva, a credible $50M Series A led by DST Global and Balderton, and senior engineering roles posted in NYC at strong comp ($220K-$300K), which is a good signal for an engineer evaluating leverage. It scores well but not top-tier because the team is already fairly large (~80-90), the roster of open roles is GTM-heavy, and the HQ is in Belgium rather than the US.
assessment.summary: Conveo is a Belgium-founded, YC-backed AI market-research startup that automates consumer interviews and analysis; it just raised a $50M Series A (Sept 2026) led by DST Global and Balderton Capital, on top of a $5.3M 2025 seed. It has real enterprise traction and a technical CTO, but is headquartered outside the US and already has a fairly sizable (~80-90 person) team.
assessment.product: An AI platform that conducts multilingual video/voice consumer interviews and analyzes the resulting video/audio/text at scale, compressing traditional market research timelines from weeks to hours; used by product, marketing, and research teams as well as market-research agencies.
assessment.team: CEO Dieter De Mesmaeker previously founded and built DataCamp (edtech) over 13 years. Co-founder Hendrik Van Hove (26) previously worked at McKinsey. CTO Maarten joined as a founding engineer in 2024 and became CTO in 2025; he was previously CTO of Inflights, Director of Engineering at Farmgirl Flowers, and an Engineering Manager at DataCamp. ~80-90 employees across Antwerp, London, and New York offices.
assessment.funding: $5.3M seed (March 2025) backed by Y Combinator, 6 Degrees Capital, Entourage Capital, Pitchdrive, and Syndicate One. $50M Series A (Sept 2026) led by DST Global Partners and Balderton Capital, with participation from Visionaries, 6 Degrees Capital, and Y Combinator. Total raised ~$55.8M.
redFlags: HQ in Antwerp, Belgium, not the US.
Engineering roles are outnumbered by sales/GTM/ops roles in current job postings.
greenFlags: CEO is a proven repeat founder (built DataCamp into a major edtech company).
Real enterprise traction: 400+ enterprise customers, 50+ Fortune 500, including Google, Unilever, AB InBev, and Canva.
Reputable lead investors (DST Global, Balderton Capital) and YC backing since seed.
Senior Product Engineer roles posted in NYC (a preferred location) with strong compensation, indicating real engineering investment.
CTO has relevant prior technical leadership experience (CTO of Inflights, Director of Engineering at Farmgirl Flowers).

name: Creoir

The Swedish VC fund is leading Creoir’s ongoing Seed round that has a €2 million target. The company plans to use this capital to accelerate the commercialisation of the EdgeVUI and Operator Assistant products […] The post Oulu-based Creoir…

assessment.whatTheyDo: Creoir builds embedded/offline voice AI (speech recognition, TTS, voice assistants) for defence and mission-critical systems, sold to European defence primes.
concerns: Core business is voice AI explicitly for defence/mission-critical military systems (partners include Saab, Leidos, TKMS, and a NATO counter-UAS initiative) — this falls squarely in the person's 'actively not interested in: defense and weapons systems' category.
Headquartered in Oulu, Finland — outside the US, with no evidence of a US presence, materially harder to join given the person's US/CA/NY/WA/MA + remote-in-US preference.
No open roles or careers page found, so there's no signal on hiring seniority or engineering openness.

assessment.rationale: Although Creoir has real shipped products (EdgeVUI, Operator Assistant) and named defence-industry customers, the entire business is defence/mission-critical voice AI — a category the person explicitly excludes — and the company is based in Finland with no evident US hiring. assessment.summary: Creoir is an Oulu, Finland-based company (founded 2012) that builds embedded/offline voice AI and speech recognition technology, now focused on defence and mission-critical systems for customers like Saab, Leidos, and TKMS. assessment.product: EdgeVUI (offline/edge automatic speech recognition, NLU, TTS for hands-free operator control of mission-critical systems) and Operator Assistant (AI knowledge-base assistant answering mission-status and system queries in real time).
assessment.team: Three co-founders with 10+ years in speech recognition/voice assistants, formerly from the mobile phone industry: Antti Lilja (CEO), Jaakko Mattila (COO), Oskari Ketola (CTO). Company reported to have around 11 employees.
assessment.funding: Seed round (target €2M) led by Gungnir Capital (Swedish VC), announced ~2026-09-04; company previously raised seed funding from Butterfly Ventures in 2022. Also received EU/ERDF grant support.
redFlags: Defence/military end-use is a stated anti-interest for this person, not just an adjacent risk.
No US presence or remote-in-US hiring evidence found.
No careers page or open engineering roles surfaced despite searching.
greenFlags: Real, shipped, deployed products with named enterprise/defence customers (Saab, Leidos, TKMS) rather than vaporware.
Small team (~11 people) with technically deep, founder-CTO-led leadership and over a decade of domain expertise in speech tech.

name: Félix

Summary: Félix, a Miami-based AI-powered WhatsApp remittance platform for Latino immigrants, announced on Tuesday that it has secured $200 million in Series C funding co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and General Catalyst.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Félix runs an AI-powered WhatsApp chatbot that lets Latino immigrants in the U.S. send remittances to family across Latin America, using stablecoin rails under the hood.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: At ~$1.4B valuation with ~$300M raised across three rounds, the team is almost certainly well past the small, high-leverage stage this person prefers.

Neither founder appears to be a hands-on technical operator today: Godoy has a Caltech EE background but has spent recent years in business/MBA roles; García's background is McKinsey, Uber, and Waymo market-expansion, not core engineering — no named technical co-founder or CTO surfaced.

The product runs on stablecoin/blockchain rails (a16z's crypto arm co-invested), which sits adjacent to the crypto/web3 category this person explicitly wants to avoid, even though the company itself is a fintech product, not a token play.
HQ is Miami, not one of the person's preferred states (CA/NY/WA/MA), and several open engineering roles found were remote-in-Brazil rather than U.S.-based.
assessment.rationale: Strong thematic fit — applied AI in a real fintech vertical with a live product processing $8B+ in transfers and 2.5x YoY revenue growth, and it is actively hiring Senior/Staff engineers, which is a good signal. But it's a $200M Series C unicorn with founders who read as business-oriented rather than deep technical builders, and its stablecoin infrastructure brushes against a category the person said to avoid — so it lands as a solid but not exceptional match rather than a drop-everything one.
assessment.summary: Félix (Felix Pago) is a Miami-based, venture-backed fintech that turns WhatsApp into a remittance channel for Latino immigrants sending money to ~10-11 Latin American countries, just closing a $200M Series C ($87M equity led by a16z, $113M debt from General Catalyst) at roughly unicorn valuation.
